The build process uses standard Perl module installation commands (`Makefile.PL`, `make`, `make install`) with appropriate environment variables to ensure files are installed under `$pkgdir` and into the correct vendor directories. There are no signs of obfuscated code, unexpected network operations, or unauthorized system modifications.

The package depends on other Perl modules, all of which appear to be related to web framework functionality (e.g., database interaction, templating, JSON/XML handling), consistent with the description of "a MVC web framework". No dangerous commands such as `curl|bash`, `eval`, or base64-encoded payloads are present. The use of `export` in build and check phases is limited to standard Perl environment variables for non-interactive module installation. The file ends with editor settings, which are harmless.

While the source uses plain HTTP instead of HTTPS, this is common in older CPAN-based packages and does not constitute a supply-chain attack by itself, especially since the integrity of the download is verified via strong checksums (SHA512). No evidence of data exfiltration, remote code execution, or malicious behavior was found.
</details>

The source is fetched from `search.cpan.org`, which is the official CPAN mirror and a legitimate source for Perl distributions. There are no signs of malicious activity in this file. It does not execute code, make unexpected network requests, or modify system files. The dependencies listed are consistent with a Perl-based MVC framework and are all prefixed with `perl-`, indicating they are standard Perl modules. The use of `!emptydirs` is a common packaging option to prevent empty directories from being created during packaging, which is benign. No scripts or commands are present in this file — it is purely declarative metadata.

While the source URL uses HTTP instead of HTTPS, this is a known limitation of older CPAN mirrors and is common in AUR packages for Perl modules. However, the presence of strong checksums (SHA-512) mitigates the risk of tampering during transit. This file does not contain any obfuscated code, unexpected behaviors, or supply-chain attack vectors.
</details>
